additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: Minor consistency note (not a spelling issue): the `checks` array entries here use heterogeneous key sets — the first four entries use `command`/`recorded_at`/`ctest_passed`/`local_receipt`, the Python-test entries use `tests`/`log`, and the ruff entries use neither (one has a bare `files` key). Additionally, `evidence/reconciliation.json` uses a different convention for the same concept (`name`/`cases_or_suites`/`receipt`). No keys are misspelled, but if any tooling parses these evidence files generically, aligning on one key convention per schema would make consumption more robust.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: Distinct dated evidence schemas intentionally retain their original per-check metadata; no generic parser is claimed. Missing historical timestamps are explicitly null. Renaming heterogeneous historical measurements would invent uniformity.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: `snooze()` (and `acknowledge()`, which delegates to it) bypasses the state and validity guards that `respond()` enforces: there is no `ready()`/epoch check and no `valid_id()` validation. As a result a caller can mutate `not_before` on `stale` or `responding` entries, or while the state is fully desynchronized. Such mutations are then silently ignored by `ordered()` (which only surfaces `RequestStatus::pending` entries), masking adapter misuse that the revision/epoch guards elsewhere were designed to catch. Consider validating the ID and returning `false` when `!ready()` or when the entry is not in `pending` status, consistent with `respond()`.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: Addressed in a87eb86: local scheduling now requires ready state and pending status. IDs not present cannot mutate state.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: Redundant assignment: `sequence_ = position.sequence;` is executed here immediately after the capability/watermark checks, and then again verbatim on the success path at the end of the function. On the success path the first write is dead; on early-return paths (`desynchronized`) `desynchronize()` already leaves the state stale, so the early write only serves as a watermark advance. Either drop the first assignment or add a comment clarifying that it intentionally raises the watermark even when reconciliation fails, since having two identical writes is confusing about which one is authoritative.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: Addressed in a87eb86: removed the redundant later assignment; the initial assignment intentionally advances the failure watermark.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: `contract_version` currently has no consumers anywhere in the codebase (verified by search). If it is intended as the versioning hook for future wire serialization, consider documenting that intent in a comment; otherwise it is dead surface area in the public header.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: contract_version is the public standalone reducer contract marker for adapters integrating this checkpoint; no serialization is implemented or claimed. Retained as the agreed interface version.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: Asymmetric ID validity: `valid_id()` accepts any `std::int64_t` (including `0` and negative values, which are common sentinel choices) while rejecting empty strings. If `0`/negative integer IDs are meant to be invalid just like empty strings, the check should handle the integer alternative explicitly; otherwise a short comment on why only string emptiness is rejected would help readers.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: Integer IDs are source identities, not local sentinels. Zero and negative signed IDs are valid protocol values; only empty/oversized string identities are rejected. Preserving source types is a repository contract.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: The sort comparator recomputes `score()` (including an integer division by `aging_interval`) for both elements on every comparison, which is O(n log n) redundant work and relies on the comparator being a strict weak ordering over values derived from mutable state. With the default `pending` limit of 128 this is minor, but precomputing the score once per element (e.g. sorting a vector of `{score, arrived, id}` tuples or decorating before sorting) would be clearer and cheaper, and removes the repeated `pending_.at()` lookups inside the comparator.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: Addressed in a87eb86: each rank is computed once before sorting.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: A duplicate `reconcile` at the same sequence (`position.sequence == sequence_` is allowed by the `<` check above) re-applies the snapshot and, at the end of the function, assigns a fresh `revision()` to *every* entry — including entries whose request payload is byte-identical and whose `arrived`/`not_before`/`submitted` are explicitly preserved. This unnecessarily invalidates an in-flight response token captured just before the re-delivery: `respond(epoch, id, old_revision, ...)` will fail even though nothing about the request changed. Since duplicate reconcile deliveries should be idempotent, consider skipping the revision bump for entries that match the preserved previous entry exactly (only new/changed entries need a fresh revision).
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: Addressed in a87eb86: identical synchronized same-epoch requests preserve revisions; stale recovery still rotates them.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: Capability gating is inconsistent: `reconcile()` refuses to run unless `capabilities_.observation` (and `reconciliation`) is set, but `request()`, `resolve()`, and `activity()` — which are also source-observation events — never check `capabilities_.observation`. A source connected with `observation=false` can still drive the entire incremental event stream and only fails on reconcile/respond. Either the observation gate should apply in `advance()` (covering all three), or the asymmetry should be documented in the header as intentional.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: Inapplicable: connect always desynchronizes. Only reconcile can establish synchronized_=true, and it requires observation and reconciliation. advance requires ready(). A non-observing source therefore cannot apply incremental events.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: `State` is implicitly copyable (all members are copyable value types). Copying a live attention state machine produces two independent instances sharing the same `session_id`/`adapter_id`/`epoch_`/`revision_`, which can then diverge silently — exactly the kind of split-brain condition this class's epoch/sequence/revision machinery is designed to prevent. Consider explicitly deleting the copy constructor/assignment (moves can remain) to make single ownership of a source connection enforced by the type, matching the 'One service-owned source connection' contract in the comment.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: This reducer is a value model with no I/O or connection handles. Copying it for deterministic replay does not duplicate a real connection; the service/adapter owns response execution. Deleting copy would not enforce source uniqueness because another State can be constructed with the same IDs.

additional_partial_kimi_findings.finding: The `ordering()` test exercises aging, snooze, and acknowledge, but never verifies the strict-weak-ordering tie-break on equal scores (same `arrived`, same priority) or the `RequestId` heterogeneity in ordering (mixed `int64_t`/`string` IDs sort by variant index before value). Since `ordered()` relies on `std::tie(a.arrived, left) < std::tie(b.arrived, right)` as the final tie-break over a `std::variant`, a small case with two equal-score requests (one integer ID, one string ID, inserted at the same tick) would pin down that the comparator is deterministic and total.
additional_partial_kimi_findings.resolution: The implementation now sorts precomputed score/arrival/id tuples with standard tuple and variant ordering. Existing replay/order tests cover deterministic ranking; this is an optional extra tie-break fixture, not a demonstrated failure.
